clean: Oh my god, I did it, I auditioned for the chamber choir tonight. I was shaking the whole time and my voice cracked on the high G in the sight-reading bit, properly cracked, but Lucesta, who runs it, said that's fine and that she was more interested in how I blend. Hi Beatrix, thanks so much for meeting with us on Thursday, it was really helpful to understand what the bank is hoping to get out of the sponsorship. To recap what we discussed, the festival would name the audience award after the bank, include your logo on all printed materials and the opening night trailer, and give you 30 complimentary passes to distribute to staff and clients. In return, the bank would contribute €15,000, Made in two installments, half on signing and half after the festival. You also mentioned that you might want a short speaking slot at the award ceremony, which we're happy to offer, though we'd ask that it's kept to about two minutes. I'll send over a draft agreement by the end of next week, once our board has had a look at it. In the meantime, let me know if I've missed anything. Yes, Bert

I just started a job as a claims assistant at a commercial insurer, not a broker, and I keep hearing terms in meetings that I'm too embarrassed to ask about. Could you explain, in plain English, the difference between a deductible and an excess, whether they're actually the same thing in different countries, and what people mean when they say a claim has been reserved? Also, my manager Torston keeps saying that a client is underinsured and that average will apply, and I nodded along, but I honestly have no idea what average means in that sentence. If you can, give me a simple example with numbers for the average thing, like a warehouse insured for half its value. And last one, what's subrogation, and why would the insurer care about it after they've already paid out? Keep each answer short, I'd rather understand the basics than get every exception.

Hi Mr. and Mrs. Hartigan, I wanted to give you an update on your installation. Unfortunately, the inverter we specified for your system has been delayed by the manufacturer, and our supplier is now quoting the end of November for delivery, rather than the first week of November as we originally hoped. I know you were keen to have everything running before winter and I'm really sorry about this.

We have two options. We can wait for the original inverter, which is the one we'd recommend because it matches your monitoring app and battery plans. Or we can switch to a comparable model that's in stock now, which would let us install on the 13th, but you'd lose the integrated battery compatibility and need an extra of the doctor later. There's no difference in price either way.

Could you let me know which you'd prefer by Friday? If you'd like to talk it through, my direct line is 0161 496 2280. Best wishes, Blucaster Rays

Attendance. We know everyone has busy lives, but the choir only works if people turn up consistently in the last month before a concert. So the rule is that you can miss up to two rehearsals in the four weeks before a performance and still sing in it. If you need to miss more than that, talk the director, I landed, as early as possible and we'll try to work something out, for example a catch-up session. Please let your section leader know if you'll be absent, even if it's last minute, a quick text is fine. And if you're unwell, especially with anything that affects your voice or might be contagious, stay home. Honestly, we'd much rather you rested than sang through a cold and passed it to the whole alto section.

Dear Mr. Casilanos, I'm writing on behalf of the four pharmacies in the Westbrook group to raise a concern about delivery times. Over the past six weeks, our morning deliveries have arrived after 11 a.m. on more than half of all days, against a contracted window of before 9. This has a real impact on patients, because prescriptions that are waiting on stock can't be collected until the afternoon, and several of our patients travel in from rural areas by bus. We've raised this with the depot on several occasions, most recently with Ludwig on the 3rd of October, but haven't seen any improvement. We'd be grateful if you could look into the routing for our area and let us know what can be done. We've attached a log of delivery times from all four branches. If the situation doesn't improve by the end of the month, we'll need to review our arrangements. Yours sincerely, Barnaby Chunderin, Operations Lead

Write a short synopsis for our festival catalogue, about 60 words, for a documentary we're screening. Here's what I know about it. It's called The Salt Road, it runs 92 minutes, and it's directed by Margery Quayle, it's her first feature. It follows two generations of a family of salt harvesters on the coast of Brittany over one summer, as the youngest daughter decides whether to stay and take over the salt pans or move to Paris for university. There's no narration, it's all observational, and the cinematography is stunning, lots of long wide shots of the marshes at dawn. I don't want the synopsis to give away what she decides. Also, avoid words like poignant and breathtaking, every single synopsis in the catalogue uses them. And give me two versions, one more lyrical and one more straightforward.

Daily log, Tuesday. Crew of four on site at the dairy farm jobs, Anselm and the two apprentices. We finished mounting the rails on the main barn roof by 11 and started placing panels after lunch. Got through 38 of the 64 panels before the wind picked up around 3 and we had to stop, gusts were over 30 miles an hour according to the app. No injuries, no damage. One issue, the barn roof has more corrosion on the purlins at the east end than the survey showed, I'd say three of them need reinforcing before we put weight on them. I've taken photos and flagged it to the engineer. The farmer was fine with us leaving equipment in the machine shed overnight. Plan for tomorrow is finish the panels if the wind drops, otherwise start the trenching for the cable run to the house.

Hi there, I'm following up on my travel insurance claim, reference TR77403. I submitted it on the 5th of September after my flight home from Lisbon was canceled and I had to pay for three extra nights in a hotel and a new flight, which came to €640 in total. I've already sent the cancellation email from the airline, the hotel receipts and my bank statement showing the new flight, so I'm not sure what else is needed. If there's something missing, could you please tell me exactly what it is so I can send it straight away? I'd also appreciate an estimate of when I can expect a decision. Thanks for your help, Cormac Doyle

I'd like some RS device, not a pep talk. I'm 38, I've worked in insurance claims for about 15 years, and I'm good at it, but I'm completely bored. For the past two years I've been working weekends at a friend's bike shop, mostly doing wheel builds and basic repairs, and it's the only part of my week I actually look forward to. The owner, Idris, is retiring in two years and has hinted that he's selling the business, but I've never run anything and I have a mortgage and two kids. I'm not asking you to tell me what to do. What I want is a list of the questions I should be able to answer before I even have a serious conversation with him, about the finances, about my family, and about whether I'd still love fixing bikes if it was my whole job. This winter we're trying something new at the shop. Every Thursday evening from November through February, we'll be running a free basic maintenance class, limited to eight people a night because that's how many work stands we have. We'll cover fixing a flat, adjusting brakes, cleaning and lubing your chain, and how to tell when something's worn out and needs replacing, not just adjusting. You don't need any experience, and you don't need to have bought your bike from us, honestly we'd love to see some of the bikes that have been sitting in people's sheds since the pandemic. Bring your own bike if you can, and if you can't, Marjorie has a couple of loaners. Sign up at the counter or on our website at spokeandsprocket.co.uk/classes. The classes start at 7 and run for about an hour and a half.

Hi Lucas, following up on our conversation about the delivery van. I've looked at the numbers for the last quarter, and our home delivery service is now doing around 130 drops a week, up from about 80 this time last year. The van is doing fine mechanically, but we're running out of time in the day, the driver is regularly finishing after 6 and we've had a couple of complaints about late deliveries of things people need that evening, like antibiotics.

I think we have three realistic options. We could add a second part-time driver for the afternoon, we could move to two delivery rounds a day with a cutoff at noon, or we could partner with the courier service the other branch uses. I'd lean towards the two rounds, because it costs the least and it fixes the late afternoon problem. Happy to talk it through on Monday. Best, And so
